draft.title: The aerobic system
card: The aerobic system makes ATP using oxygen. It breaks down carbohydrates and fats, which the body takes from food and stores.
It is slow to start, because oxygen must reach the muscles first. It makes ATP at a lower rate than the other two systems.
It can keep going for hours, because the body holds large stores of fuel, especially fat. It does not build up the by-products linked to fatigue in hard efforts.
It supplies most of the energy in long, steady activity, such as a distance run, a long swim or a bushwalk.
draft.remember: Aerobic: oxygen and fuel from food and stores give slow, lasting ATP.

a.q: Why can the aerobic system supply energy for hours?
opts: It uses oxygen and large fuel stores to make ATP
It uses a store of ATP that is very large
It makes ATP faster than any other system
It breaks down glucose without needing oxygen
a.why: The aerobic system uses oxygen with carbohydrates and fats, and the body holds large stores of these, especially fat. It does not make ATP faster than the other systems, which is why it suits steady effort rather than explosive effort.
a.clue: Think about what fuel it uses and how much the body holds.

b.q: Priya walks for four hours on a flat bush track at a steady pace. Which system supplies most of her energy?
opts: All of her energy comes from stored ATP
b.why: A long, steady effort relies on the aerobic system, which uses oxygen and can last for hours. The body has only a little stored ATP, so it could not power four hours of walking.
b.clue: Look at how long and how hard the effort is.

a.best: It uses oxygen and large fuel stores to make ATP
